source_caption:
To achieve the illusion that The Holdovers was not merely set in 1970 but actively filmed then, director Alexander Payne and cinematographer Eigil Bryld employed a meticulous, reverse-engineered post-production process. Though principal photography was captured entirely on modern digital ARRI Alexa cameras to manage the harsh, snowy New England shooting conditions, the pristine digital files were subjected to a rigorous degradation process. The team intentionally added custom film grain, gate weave (the slight mechanical jitter of film moving through a projector), emulsion halation around light sources, and artificial dust and scratches. Payne carried this obsessive commitment to the era’s aesthetic into the audio mix by eschewing modern surround sound in favor of a flat, vintage mono track, and even commissioned bespoke, 1970s-style retro studio logos for Focus Features and Miramax to play before the opening credits, completely immersing the audience in the illusion of a rediscovered cinematic relic.

The Holdovers (2023), directed by Alexander Payne, starring Paul Giamatti, Da’Vine Joy Randolph, Dominic Sessa. A curmudgeonly, universally disliked history teacher at a prestigious New England boarding school is forced to remain on campus during the 1970 Christmas break to supervise a grieving, rebellious student, leading to an unexpected bond with the school’s head cook who recently lost her son in Vietnam.

source_details.synopsis: The Holdovers is a 2023 American Christmas comedy drama film directed by Alexander Payne, written by David Hemingson, and starring Paul Giamatti, Da'Vine Joy Randolph, and Dominic Sessa in his film debut. Set in 1970, it tells the story of a strict classics teacher at a New England boarding school who is forced to chaperone a handful of students who have nowhere to go during the school's Christmas holiday break. Filming took place from January to March 2022 in Massachusetts. The Holdovers premiered at the 50th Telluride Film Festival on August 31, 2023, and was released in the United States by Focus Features on October 27, 2023.
